title: How to pick between packs, and when core already does it
hook: Most searches for a pack should end in core. A short ladder: does core do it, what does the gap really need, is the code what you think, and can you live with its side effects?

verified.claim: Core has PerturbedAttentionGuidance, EasyCache, LazyCache, ImageGrid and ImageCompare. ImageGrid takes images, columns, cell sizes and padding.
verified.ref: the server's read-only object_info and the source

verified.claim: sd-perturbed-attention is MIT and has pag_nodes.py and tpg_nodes.py, with its own PerturbedAttention and TokenPerturbationGuidance classes.
verified.ref: the pack's LICENSE and files, read as text and not run

verified.claim: ComfyUI-MiniMaxH3-FirstBlockCache is MIT, works by first-block residual, and its README reports 1.44× to 1.49× and calls itself an approximation.
verified.ref: the pack's LICENSE, nodes.py and README, read as text

verified.claim: ComfyUI-SweepGrid is MIT with nodes for sweep combinations and video grids.
verified.ref: the pack's LICENSE and nodes folder, read as text

verified.claim: All three are on our hand-read pick list, as candidates for a sandbox test.

unchecked: We didn't run any of these packs for this lesson. Being on our list means someone read it, not that it works for you.
The speed figure is the pack author's own. We didn't test it.
The 2% in the lab is an example for the arithmetic, not a measured rate.
Other good packs do these jobs. We read only these.
